text:
The Penguins arrive in Buffalo winless in five and outscored 20-9 in that stretch, and the conversation around them has moved from the standings to the trade market. Josh Yohe's reporting, as relayed by several outlets this week, has Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell close to being moved; Ottawa's interest keeps coming up; the Wild were linked to Evgeni Malkin after missing on Dylan Larkin. Sidney Crosby's future is in the headlines too. With 16 points from 24 games and a 4.5% playoff chance by our race simulations, it is easy to see why.

The frustrating part for Pittsburgh is that the hockey is not as bad as the record. At five on five they have taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) this season, and two of the five losses in this skid came in games they won on chances. The finishing and the goaltending have not followed. Sergei Murashov starts tonight over Arturs Silovs; he is 2.5 goals below expected this season. Bryan Rust is out until early December, which has pushed Malkin up beside Crosby and Rakell, and Malkin had two power-play points in his return on Wednesday.

Buffalo is 3-2 in its last five and coming off a 5-1 win over the Rangers in which Rasmus Dahlin scored 17 seconds in. Tage Thompson has nine points in a five-game streak and Jack Quinn has goals in four straight, both running hotter than their chances, so some cooling is normal. The Sabres are without Zach Benson and Noah Ostlund, which pushes Quinn and Josh Doan up the lineup, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen starts. One thing Pittsburgh can use: Buffalo takes 4.0 penalties a game.

Our numbers lean Buffalo at home, 3.50 expected goals to 3.16. Our sleeper is Jason Zucker, a third-liner with dangerous shots lately (1.9 expected goals in his last ten) against his old team: 22% to score, by our numbers.
headline: Penguins bring a five-game skid and a trade cloud
